assessments.reasoning: The archived Module Details explicitly say each call creates new symbols and substitutes them into the body, excluding locally scoped occurrences. Nested Modules and exported local symbols receive separate statements.

challenge.method: Compare two calls returning their local symbol, a nested same-name binder, and a called definition reading an external symbol. Read Block alongside the archived modularity tutorial to challenge a dynamic-scope interpretation and inspect Module's rules on returned local symbols.
challenge.results: The fresh symbols and lexical substitution follow the published rule. The nested local binder's occurrences are protected from the outer substitution. The contrast example depends on the symbol in a called definition and does not extend substitution beyond the Module body. The reference allows a local symbol to be returned, so the rule supplies no general disposal guarantee.

limitations: The claim leaves generated-name counters, initializer order and symbol lifetime outside its scope. Its ordinary documented substitution rule is independent of whether later evaluation is symbolic or numerical.
